title: Compliance Memorandum — Statutory Release from a Lease Term Agreement
content:
A statutory release ends a fixed Lease Term Agreement early without any early termination fee, reletting fee, concession recapture or lease-break rent.

## 1. Grounds

| Ground | Who and what |
|---|---|
| Military orders | The resident or spouse enters military service or receives permanent change of station or deployment orders of ninety days or more. |
| Domestic violence | The resident or a household member is a victim and provides the qualifying court order or report of the community's state. |
| Death of the sole leaseholder | Requested by the estate. |

## 2. Documentation

A statutory release is granted only when the community manager has recorded the qualifying document against the request; the resident's statement alone never grants it. The request record's type and its stated statutory ground show what has been recorded. A release that is not documented is handled as an Early Termination Option or a lease break.

## 3. Effective dates

| Ground | The release takes effect |
|---|---|
| Military orders | 30 calendar days after the first rent due date following delivery of the written notice with the orders |
| Domestic violence — California | 14 calendar days after delivery of the notice |
| Domestic violence — Washington, Colorado, Texas, Georgia, Arizona | 30 calendar days after delivery of the notice |
| Death of the sole leaseholder | 30 calendar days after the estate's written notice |

## 4. Rent and deposit

Rent keeps posting under the Apartment Home Lease rules through the release date, and the security deposit is accounted for under the Security Deposit Account rules as on any move-out.

## Illustrations (hypothetical dates)

- Orders delivered with written notice on 12 May, rent due on the first of each month: the first rent due date after delivery is 1 June, and the release takes effect 30 calendar days after it, on 1 July.
- A domestic violence notice delivered in California on 3 October with the qualifying court order recorded: the release takes effect 14 calendar days later, on 17 October. In Arizona the same notice takes effect on 2 November.
- A resident states by phone that they have received deployment orders but no document is recorded against the request: no statutory release is granted.
